skeleton: frog sitting facing the viewer: root at the seat; body (head and body are one) with belly squash and a throat/chin to puff; eyes in the two domes on top, mouth below; front legs at the shoulders; folded back legs at the hips; tongue (hidden until it flicks out from the mouth, stretching) and a little fly on its own bone for the catch-fly.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a frog character. Draw this exact frog as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the round green spotted frog with its cream belly, sitting and facing the viewer as in image 1, with the two big eye domes on top, without front legs or back legs, and with a completely blank face — the eye domes empty and green with no eyes in them, no mouth — keep the rosy cheeks.
2. one front leg: the front leg on the right of image 1 with its spread webbed toes, with a rounded shoulder.
3. one back leg: the folded back leg on the right of image 1 with its long webbed foot, with a rounded hip.
4. the tongue: a long pink tongue, straight, on its own, with a rounded tip.
5. a little fly: a tiny cute fly with clear wings.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a frog character; image 2 shows the same frog cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the frog's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the frog in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the frog's left eye (on the right of image 1) as it is in image 1: a big dark round eye with a white sparkle, filling its eye dome.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same eye sad: looking down, its upper lid tilted up towards the middle.
6. the mouth as it is in image 1: a wide-open happy smile, the inside pink.
7. the mouth closed in a wide calm smile.
8. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink.
9. the mouth open in a small round 'o'.
10. the mouth in a small sad frown.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: a little fly buzzes up above the frog, who watches it very still; then its long tongue flicks out, catches the fly, and it gulps and grins.

pause.shows: the frog perfectly still, eyes locked on a little fly buzzing just above it

the frog puffs out its throat and croaks, ribbit, ribbit, ribbit.
the frog crouches low, then leaps high up into the air, legs stretched out, and lands with a squash.

the frog looks one way, then the other, then back.
the frog laughs and laughs, bouncing with giggles.

the frog talks, its mouth moving, its head bobbing a little.
